sentences.text:
1  Government Advocate (Crl.
 For R2 : Mr.S.Saravana Kumar  ORDER
This Criminal Original Petition has been filed to call for the records and quash the proceedings in C.C.No.70 of 2022 on the file of the Judicial Magistrate No-1, Vridhachalam.

2. The case of the prosecution is that the petitioners had promised to construct a house for the defacto complainant, based on which the defacto complainant had given a sum of Rs.10,15,000/- to the 1st petitioner.
Thereafter, the petitioners have cheated the defacto complainant and abused him with filthy language.

Hence, the defacto complainant has given a complaint before the 1st respondent police against the petitioners herein for the offence punishable under Sections 420,
294(b) and 506(i) of IPC in Crime No.133 of 2021.

Subsequently, https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis the 1st respondent police has conducted the investigation and filed a final report before the learned Judicial Magistrate No.1-, Vridhachalam, in C.C.No.70 of 2022.

Challenging the said final report,
the petitioner have approached this Court to quash the proceedings.

3. The learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that originally the property was belongs to the 1st petitioner and the oral partition was held in the family members with regard to division of the said properties.

He further submitted that there was a dispute between the parties, thereby, the defacto complainant filed a suit in O.S.No.208 of 2021 before the Principal Sub Court,
Chidambaram for the relief of partition and other consequential reliefs.

He further submitted that the 1st and 2nd petitioner is the father and mother of the defacto complainant and 3rd petitioner is the brother and 4th petitioner is the sister-in-law of the defacto complainant.
He further submitted that there was family dispute between the parties.
Hence, he prayed to quash the proceedings.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
4. Heard the learned Governement Advocate (Cr.Side) appearing for the 1st respondent police.

5. The learned counsel for the second respondent submitted that the second respondent has given a money to the 1st petitioner and thereafter, the petitioners have cheated the defacto complainant/second respondent.
Hence, he prayed for dismissal of this petition.
6. On a perusl of the records, it reveals that the petitioners and the second respondent are close relatives, there was a civil dispute between the petitioners and the defacto complainant.
Further, the defacto complainant filed a suit before the trial Court with regard to partition and other consequential reliefs.
Therefore, this Court is of the view that the dispute is civil in nature, thus Civil dispute has been given criminal colour.

Hence, this Court is inclined to quash the proceedings in C.C.No.70 of 2022 on the file of the Judicial Magistrate No-1, Vridhachalam.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 7.
In the result, this Criminal Original Petition is allowed.
Consequently, connected miscellaneous petition is closed.
No costs.
